title: NEURODEGENERATION, INFANTILE-ONSET, WITH OPTIC ATROPHY AND STRUCTURAL BRAIN ABNORMALITIES 2

relationships.phenotype: NEURODEGENERATION, INFANTILE-ONSET, WITH OPTIC ATROPHY AND STRUCTURAL BRAIN ABNORMALITIES 2

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities-2 (NDOABA2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the BORCS5 gene (616598) on chromosome 12p13.2.

checks.claim: Infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities-2 (NDOABA2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the BORCS5 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Trio exome sequencing identified a homozygous c.283 C>T; p.(Arg95Ter) variant in exon 3 of the BORCS5 gene (NM_058169.4) in each of the couple's fetuses
checks.explanation: The paper links homozygous BORCS5 variants to neuroaxonal dystrophy with osteopetrosis. It never uses the NDOABA2 name, and it reports an association rather than proven causation.

checks.claim: The BORCS5 gene is located on chromosome 12p13.2.
checks.evidence_quote: a novel biallelic nonsense homozygous variant in BORCS5
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene the paper names.

paragraphs.text: Fisher et al. (2025) described this disorder as neuroaxonal dystrophy with osteopetrosis. In 2 affected sibs, prenatal imaging showed cerebral ventriculomegaly and agenesis of the corpus callosum. At autopsy, the sibs had facial dysmorphism, osteopetrosis, and neuropathologic findings consistent with neuroaxonal dystrophy.

checks.evidence_quote: Neuroaxonal dystrophy (NAD) with osteopetrosis syndrome (OMIM # 600329) was first reported in a consanguineous Moroccan Jewish family.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the disorder as NAD with osteopetrosis.

paragraphs.text: Fisher et al. (2025) studied 2 sibs, born to consanguineous Pakistani parents, who had neuroaxonal dystrophy with osteopetrosis. Using trio exome sequencing, they identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in exon 3 of the BORCS5 gene (c.283C-T, NM_058169.4), resulting in an arg95-to-ter (R95X) substitution. Each parent was heterozygous for the mutation.

paragraphs.text: Fisher et al. (2025) also found that 1 of the 2 affected sibs was homozygous for a missense variant of uncertain significance in the SCYL2 gene (616365): c.902G-A (NM_017988.5), resulting in an arg301-to-his (R301H) substitution. Both parents were heterozygous for this variant. Because the autopsy findings in the 2 sibs were identical, the authors raised the possibility that the SCYL2 variant did not contribute to the phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Fisher et al. (2025) studied 2 sibs, born to consanguineous Pakistani parents, who had neuroaxonal dystrophy with osteopetrosis (NDOABA2). In both sibs they identified a homozygous c.283C-T transition (NM_058169.4) in exon 3 of the BORCS5 gene, resulting in an arg95-to-ter (R95X) substitution. The mutation was found by trio exome sequencing, and each parent was heterozygous for it.
